title: I have been pretending to like my best friend’s cooking for six years
body: Every Sunday she makes the same dry chicken and I tell her it is the best meal of my week. She beams. I have never had the heart to say anything, and at this point the lie has more history than some of my relationships. Tonight she asked if I wanted the recipe and I said yes so fast I think I hurt her feelings.

title: Our “transparent” office raised prices and blamed the customers for noticing
body: The pricing page changed at 2am on a Tuesday. Same product, same tier, 40% more. The email we all got said it was due to “market conditions”, but the slide deck that leaked into the shared drive lists “revenue capture on low-price-sensitivity cohorts” as the actual reason. I removed the names and the deck link on purpose. Screenshots are with a journalist I trust.

title: I keep a folder of every nice thing anyone has said to me
body: Screenshots, texts, a few sticky notes I photographed before they got thrown away. It is 340 files now. I open it on bad nights. I have never told anyone because it feels pathetic, but it works better than any app I have tried.

title: I quit the job I loved because my manager started copying my ideas out loud
body: Three meetings in a row, my suggestion came out of his mouth forty minutes later as his own. I stopped speaking. Six weeks after I left, the project stalled and he emailed to ask what I had planned. I sent a one-word reply: “notes.”

title: The gym that charges you to cancel, and the fake “coach” they assign you
body: Signed up in March, cancelled in June, still being billed in November. The cancellation form on their site returns a 500 error. The “coach” who calls to save your membership has been three different people with the same name and the same script. I have the invoices, the error logs and the call recordings. Names of individual staff removed — the company is the problem, not the teenager on the phone.

title: I read my partner’s diary once and I have been a better person since
body: Two years ago I opened it looking for proof of something I was sure was happening. It was not happening. What was in there was a very long, very patient list of things I do that make them feel small. I never told them I read it. I just stopped doing all of it. We are better now, on a foundation I do not deserve.

title: My cat is not a rescue, I found him behind a restaurant and made up a story
body: Told everyone he came from a shelter in Bandung with a tragic backstory. He was eating discarded satay. His name is Kevin and he has never been tragic in his life.

title: A “charity” run by a friend’s cousin that has never donated anything
body: Public bank statements posted monthly, all screenshots, all suspiciously round numbers. The orphanage they name has no record of them. I am not naming anyone until a journalist looks; I am posting this because two people have already asked me privately whether it is real. It is not. Do not give them money.
